items.followUp: Explain how a covalent bond is formed.

rubric.description: Identifies electron sharing as the bonding process.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electrons are shared.

rubric.why: A covalent bond involves one or more pairs of electrons shared between atoms.
rubric.description: Identifies the electron pairs and the atoms involved.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying that electron pairs are shared between atoms.

modelAnswer: A covalent bond is formed when two atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.

items.followUp: What is a polar covalent bond? Give an example.

rubric.why: In a nonpolar covalent bond, the bonding electrons are shared equally.
rubric.description: Defines a nonpolar covalent bond by equal sharing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the bonding electrons are shared equally.

rubric.why: H₂, Cl₂, N₂ and O₂ are examples of nonpolar covalent molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving a correct example such as H₂ or Cl₂.

modelAnswer: A nonpolar covalent bond is a covalent bond in which the bonded atoms share the electron pair equally.
An example is the bond in an H₂ molecule.

items.followUp: Define reduction in terms of oxygen and give an example.

rubric.why: In terms of oxygen, oxidation is the addition of oxygen to a substance.
rubric.description: Defines oxidation in terms of oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that oxygen is added to a substance.

rubric.why: Magnesium reacts with oxygen to form magnesium oxide.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of oxidation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example, such as magnesium reacting with oxygen to form magnesium oxide.

modelAnswer: Oxidation, in terms of oxygen, is the addition of oxygen to a substance.
